description: This horizontal stacked bar chart illustrates the average rate at which a model attends most to specific input segments—context, generated response, or other—during generation. The vertical axis displays the categorical models being evaluated, ordered from bottom to top as "Standard" and "Ours," without an explicit overall axis title. The horizontal axis represents the value as a percentage; it lacks an explicit axis line, label, tick marks, or numerical interval, but the stacked segments implicitly span a total range of 0% to 100% for each category. Each horizontal bar is stacked with three distinct color-coded segments visually arranged from left to right. A legend at the bottom identifies these components: the blue segment represents "Context," the orange segment represents "Generated Response," and the green segment represents "Other." Every segment is visually emphasized by a direct annotation of its exact percentage, using white text within the blue segments and black text within the orange and green segments. For the "Standard" model, the segments measure 23.6% for Context, 51.1% for Generated Response, and 25.3% for Other. For the "Ours" model, the Context segment is the longest in the chart at 60.6%, followed by Generated Response at 31.7%, and Other at 7.7%, which constitutes the shortest segment overall. The bars do not follow a numerical or alphabetical sorting order, but rather present the baseline "Standard" category below the "Ours" category.
